content:
sarah: Heads up — starting the quarterly access review today. Planning a batch prune of admin entitlements for stale principals, but want gating criteria and audit signal clarified before we run it. Tagging @alex for KMS impact, @jordan for rollout/runbook, @maria for compliance evidence. TL;DR: can we safely revoke admin roles en masse if last activity > 180 days and owner is null?

alex: Short answer: maybe. Long answer: don’t touch principals that have active KMS grants or cross-account bindings. Need to exclude service identities used by infra automation and any principal with HSM/asymmetric keys. Example exclude query we should run first:
```sql
SELECT principal, role, last_active, has_kms_grant
FROM access_snapshot
WHERE role ILIKE '%admin%'
  AND last_active < TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 180 DAY)
  AND owner IS NULL;
```
This gives us the candidate set. We should join with kms_grants to drop ones with active grants.

jordan: Runbook/guardrails notes: do not do a single bulk revoke. Phased canary: batches of 10 -> 50 -> 200. After each batch verify: 1) no customer-facing errors reported, 2) auth failures are showing in audit logs, 3) rollback takes <2h. I'll add a dry-run mode that writes the planned actions to the audit bucket. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/access-prune (will add canary checklist).

maria: From compliance POV we need 3 artifacts for each revocation: decision justification, owner notification proof (email/Slack), and the audit event showing the role removal. Retention for evidence = 365 days. Also flag any principal that has an ongoing support ticket — do not prune.

audit-bot: Found 82 candidates matching the initial filter (role contains 'admin', last_active >180d, owner is null). Exporting candidate list to s3://sec-exports/access-prune/1738523410-candidates.csv

sam: Product note: some customers have ephemeral admin arrangements (30d windows). For developer/team exceptions, prefer a suspend flow that keeps ACLs attached but prevents console actions (so service hooks don't break). Suggest adding a `suspend_admin(principal)` option to the automation and an exceptions webhook for product/customer requests.

alex: KMS specifics — exclude any principal that appears in kms_grants with state = 'ACTIVE' OR grants where grant_type IN ('cross-account', 'external-hsm'). Pseudo-SQL to enforce:
```sql
AND NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM kms_grants g
  WHERE g.principal = access_snapshot.principal
    AND g.state = 'ACTIVE'
    AND g.grant_type IN ('cross-account','external-hsm')
)
```
If we remove an admin that still has active grants, re-binding failovers could be painful.

jamie: I can own the canary tomorrow morning. Proposed steps:
1) pick 10 internal dev principals (non-prod)
2) run automation with `--dry-run` and `--suspend` flags to preview
3) run actual `suspend_admin` on that batch (not full revoke)
4) monitor logs/traces and pager errors for 4 hours
5) if green, escalate to 50.
Will create a check-in thread in eng-oncall and eng-sre for monitoring cadence.

sarah: Great — owners: @jamie will run canary, @alex will validate KMS exclude list, @maria will prepare the evidence template, @jordan will update runbook and rollback scripts. I'll open the automation PR with a dry-run default. Please ack with :thumbsup: or any blockers.

jordan: :thumbsup: I'll add the rollback script that rebinds temporary roles and logs everything to the audit bucket.

alex: +1 — I'll push a join table of kms_grants -> principals to the staging query so the candidate CSV excludes risky entries.

maria: ack — working on evidence checklist and retention policy. Will post template by EOD.

audit-bot: Export saved: s3://sec-exports/access-prune/1738523410-candidates.csv (82 rows).

sarah: Thanks all. If anything unexpected pops up, tag this thread. Otherwise expect the first canary tomorrow 09:00 PT.

jamie: noted — I'll post results in this thread after the canary run.

sam: FYI: I'll surface the suspend vs revoke tradeoffs in the customer-impact doc.

(reacts: jordan :thumbsup:; alex :+1:; maria :white_check_mark:)
